statement: Pia, Quinn and Rae have 70 shells altogether. Quinn has twice as many shells as Pia, and Rae has 10 more shells than Quinn. How many shells does Rae have?

choices.misconception: I found Pia's share, one block of 12, and gave that instead of Rae's.
I found Quinn's 24 shells and forgot that Rae has 10 more.
I drew Rae's bar as one block plus 10 instead of two blocks plus 10, so I split 60 into 4 blocks of 15.
I left out the extra 10 and split all 70 into 5 equal blocks of 14, then gave Rae two of them.

hints: Draw a bar for each person, starting with Pia.
Pia's bar is one block, Quinn's is two blocks, and Rae's is two blocks with an extra piece of 10. Take the extra 10 away from the total first, so that what is left is made of equal blocks only.
There are 5 blocks plus 10. So 5 blocks make 60, and one block is 12.

solutions.reliable: Pia is 1 block, Quinn is 2 blocks and Rae is 2 blocks plus 10. Altogether that is 5 blocks plus 10, which makes 70, so 5 blocks make 60 and one block is 12. Pia has 12, Quinn has 24 and Rae has 24 + 10 = 34. Check: 12 + 24 + 34 = 70. The transferable idea: in a bar model, take away the pieces that are not whole blocks first, then share what is left among the equal blocks.

whyOnTest: Bar models test whether every comparison becomes blocks in the right place, and whether the extra 10 is taken away before sharing.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
